H4 retention soak (CACHE_CAMPAIGN.md Tier 2 H4). optimus.graph.CacheSoak (probes/cache/src/optimus/graph/CacheSoak.scala), driver probes/cache/run-cache-soak.sh.
Reuses CacheHunter's spec generator (GSpec/Mat/HRt), the H2 value oracle (H2Child.check, HOracle) and H3's tracker driver, checkpoint, invalidation
and TTrack-reachability oracles (copied into SoakBInst and adapted for an unbounded run). JDK 21, entity agent + CacheDelayAgent + WorkQueue DelayAgent.
Logs: scratchpad cache-soak/ (soak-<run>-seg<k>.log per JVM segment, driver-<run>.txt), repro/ for the follow-up runs, attempt1/2 and b-lpon-* for
the discarded first launches.

================================================================ Commands (all four started 02:21-02:36, 60 min each, run concurrently; host load avg 75-85 on 18 cores from other agents)

  O="-Xmx3g -Doptimus.gthread.ideal=4 -Dprobes.delay.maxNanos=50000"          # production cacheSize (850000) untouched
  A        SOAK_OPTS="$O"                                                            probes/cache/run-cache-soak.sh a 60 1000
  B-lpoff  SOAK_TAG=lpoff     SOAK_OPTS="$O -Dhunter.off=lp"                         probes/cache/run-cache-soak.sh b 60 2000
  B-wm1    SOAK_TAG=lpoff-wm1 SOAK_OPTS="$O -Dhunter.off=lp -Doptimus.tracking.cleanup.ttrackClearedNodeRefWatermark=1"  probes/cache/run-cache-soak.sh b 60 2000
  B-lpon   SOAK_TAG=lpon      SOAK_OPTS="$O"                                         probes/cache/run-cache-soak.sh b 42 2000   (restarted 02:36 with the starvation probe)
  follow-ups (5-7 min each): same commands with -Dhunter.soakRoot=N / -Dhunter.soakNoRebase=true / -Dhunter.soakNoDispose=true / -Dhunter.off=lp,when,
  and the census/scopedTotal instrumentation (now part of every SUMMARY line).

================================================================ Design as run

A: 20 fixed H2 specs (seeds 1000..1019, 12-500 props, 2-18 scenario nodes, ~191 k (key x stack) pairs), scenario trees built ONCE on one uniqueID root
   per DAG and cycled forever by 4 client threads (random DAG/node/key, 10% under a child cancel scope cancelled after 0-3 ms). Oracle: H2Child.check.
B: 3 roots (seeds 2000, 2001, 2002: 14, 245, 365 props), each its own spec and tracker plan t0 root / t1 consistent child / t2 concurrent child /
   t3 consistent child of t2 created by the newChild action and disposed at a checkpoint (p=1/4 once >= 5 phases old), 2 clients per root, driver
   actions with a fresh RNG seed per phase (add/addAsync/batch/evaluate/async/low-priority/newChild/setPluginTag/cancellable eval). Tags on root 0
   only (tags everywhere made F8 mask everything). H3 checkpoint after every phase (clients paused, queues idle): value oracle on every recorded
   node, over/under invalidation against the previous snapshot, TTrack reachability for every valid non-XS node. To stay bounded for an hour the
   harness rebases every tracker's version history to its last state at each checkpoint, clears Mat's identity memos, removes poisoned-subtree
   tweaks (recovery; never needed: recovered=0) and reports each STALE_LATENT node once.
SUMMARY every 300 s, taken quiescent (A: clients paused + scheduler settled; B: all roots parked at a checkpoint barrier): heap after 2x System.gc(),
   global/siGlobal getSizeIndicative(true), verifyInvariants on both (WARN/ERROR counted by a logback appender; throws caught), approxNumCacheEntries,
   CacheIDs.global size, per tracker: ttracks roots, TTrack nodes reachable, ptrack edges, TTrackRefs, cleared TTrackRefs, refQ cleared counter;
   og.worker threads, _onStalledCallbacks, per-tracker workQueue/lowPriorityQueue/inFlightWork (sampled before the barrier), cumulative oracle counters.
Deviations: (1) B's key set is NOT constant: every update generates fresh tweak values, so new XSFT/XS minimum-scenario entries are legitimate (see
   finding S2); the only constant-key run is A. (2) B ran with low-priority evaluations off (B-lpoff, B-wm1) because with them on root 2 starves
   (finding S3) and the JVM died every 1-2 min before the starvation probe was added; B-lpon is the low-priority run. (3) The watermark-1 run ran
   concurrently instead of after the first hour. (4) Load from other agents throttled throughput; numbers are per-run absolute.

final oracle counters: phases=8601 checkpoints=8604 eval.checked=225106 eval.value=194254 eval.ambiguous=0 eval.skippedPoisoned=0 eval.skippedRebased=0 chk.valid=1324791 chk.validOk=1322488 inv.expected=124502 inv.over=0 inv.under=13634 inv.untouchedValid=1169982 ttrack.nodesChecked=1191531 ttrack.edgesChecked=2386719 recovered=0 trk.late=576 trk.lateDisposed=575 findings=2431

================================================================ Retention verdicts (fit over the 12 five-minute samples)

Flat for the whole hour in every JVM: CacheIDs.global (A 121, B 2-4), og.worker threads (A 3, B 4), live threads, _onStalledCallbacks (0),
   siGlobal (A 798, B 88-89), verifyInvariants (0 WARN, 0 ERROR on global and siGlobal at all 52 quiescent samples), TTrack graphs per root
   (B: roots/tracks/edges/refs oscillate 2-10 k with no trend; cleared TTrackRefs 0-337, collected by cleanup at both watermarks), recorded-node
   map (~9.6 k), tracker queues drain at every checkpoint (wq/lp/inFlight at the sample are in-flight work of running clients, max 24).
A global: 101 k -> 244.7 k, slope 24.8 k/5 min in the first half, 2.0 k in the second, last three samples 243.9/244.4/244.7 k: LEVELS OFF.
   Heap after GC 133 -> 286 MB, levels off (second-half slope 1.4 MB/5 min). Caveat: the plateau is near both the fixed key set (191 k key x stack
   pairs plus XS/XSFT proxies, 35% of entries at 5 min) and the S1 floor (212,500); scopedTotal was added after the hour-long A run, and a 5-min A
   rerun had already cut the effective cap to 556 k, so whether A saturated its key set or hit the shrinking cap is not separated.
B global: +17.0 k/5 min, linear, until it hits 212,500 (= 850,000 >> 2) at ~50 min in B-lpoff and B-wm1, then flat (B-lpon reached 211 k at 36 min, then its R6 hang). Heap +117 MB/5 min,
   1.4-1.5 GB at the cap, flat afterwards. Not a leak of entries (census: invalid entries 0-180 at any time; entries carry ~50 k distinct SSCacheIDs
   per 60 k entries: fresh XSFT minimum scenarios for fresh tweak values, unreachable after the next update and held only until LRU eviction),
   but the 212,500 cap is not the configured 850,000: see S1.

================================================================ Findings

S1 (NEW, M) NodeScopedCache size accounting leaks, so the global cache's effective capacity collapses to its 25% floor.
   NodeScopedCache.newEntryAdded increments the static LongAdder totalSize; the only decrement is resetSizeReporting(), called only from
   CacheSelector.Scoped.onOwnerReset() <- ScenarioStack.withRecorded (XS owner completion). UNodeCache.adjustedMaxSize returns
   max(maxSize/4, maxSize - totalSize) when scopedCachesReducesGlobalSize (default = scopeXSCache = true). Any scoped cache dropped without
   onOwnerReset keeps its count forever. Which drop path leaks was not pinned down; candidates are XS owners whose recording stack is abandoned
   without withRecorded (completion by exception or cancellation, or a proxy that re-runs the owner) and Scoped.newScoped(), which builds a new
   scoped cache next to the current one. Measured with scopedTotal in SUMMARY, all
   samples quiescent (no evaluation in flight, so no live scoped cache should be counted):
       B (3 roots, lpoff)  t=60 s 184 k, 121 s 465 k, 181 s 698 k, 242 s 925 k, 302 s 1,224 k;  globalMaxAdjusted 665 k -> 385 k -> 212,500 from t=181 s
       A (H2 fixed DAGs)   t=61 s  75 k, 122 s 143 k, 182 s 207 k, 244 s 254 k, 305 s   294 k;  globalMaxAdjusted 775 k -> 556 k, still falling
   Monotone, never decreases, exceeds every plausible live scoped-cache population by orders of magnitude. Effect: after minutes of XS traffic the
   global cache evicts at 212,500 instead of 850,000 for the life of the process (hit rate, not memory). Not D1-D18, F18, R6 or R14. Fix direction:
   reset (or decrement on drop) every scoped cache that leaves a selector chain, e.g. in Scoped.newScoped and on owner completion by exception or
   cancellation; or account live size via a cleaner. (repro/scoped-b.log, repro/scoped-a.log; cmd in repro/cmd-scoped-*.txt)
S2 (observation, L) B's linear growth before the cap is XSFT/XS entries for fresh tweak values (census: proxies 1-2%, TweakNodes 3%, the rest plain
   nodes under ~one SSCacheID each). Retained heap per cached entry is ~6.6 KB in B against ~1.2 KB in A; at the nominal 850 k cap that would be
   ~5.6 GB (B would OOM a 3 GB heap before the LRU caps it if S1 were fixed). Not a leak; a sizing note for tracker-heavy processes.
S3 (observation, design) Low-priority starvation. With low-priority evaluations on, root 2 (seed 2002, 365 props) never completes a driver's
   low-priority evaluation while its two clients keep issuing foreground evaluations: lowPriorityQueue holds 5-19 actions, the concurrent child's
   in-flight work keeps the parent queue busy. The soak first classified it QUEUE_STALL (7 JVM deaths in 7 segments of 1-2 min). Probe: after 20 s
   pause the clients; in all 36 occurrences (STARVED/STARVED_PROBE 32+4) the futures then completed within ~0.5 s. Starvation by foreground load,
   not a wedge. Matches the queue's documented semantics (low-priority only when the queue is otherwise idle); worth a note because nothing bounds it.

Hangs / JVM deaths (all runs, including discarded launches):
   R6        2  HANG-CLASS R6(lowPriCancel waits under queueLock; cancelled node's thread blocked in afterActionCompleted). attempt1 (5.5 min) and
                B-lpon seg0 at 38 min (og.worker blocked in afterActionCompleted:292, clients BLOCKED in registerOrEnqueueAction). Known R6, organic.
   S3        7  QUEUE_STALL root 2 phase 8/9/11 (before the starvation probe); reclassified as starvation by the probe.
   harness   1  attempt1 A: H2Child.leakDiag resolves keys through the single H2Child.curSys, which is wrong with 20 ProbeSystems in one JVM
                (ArrayIndexOutOfBounds, client threads died, watchdog). Fixed by disabling leakDiag in the soak.
   none in A (60 min), B-lpoff (60 min), B-wm1 (60 min).

   UNEXPLAINED 0; HARNESS 0; H5 not run. Counts are per request and repeat: the same stale/poisoned cache entries are hit again and again over an hour.

   invalidation oracle 1,503,695 expected, 0 over, 259,664 under-but-touched (not failures, H3 semantics), 24,029,347 untouched-valid,

================================================================ UNEXPLAINED classification (B)

ORACLE UNEXPLAINED (13/16/18 per run): wrong values almost only on the concurrent child t2 and on t3 (consistent child created by newChildScenario
   under t2), suspects RACING_UPDATE/CONC_CHILD/LATE_CHILD, roots 0 and 2. Same shape as the fuzzer's D18 report (concurrent child + late child +
   by-name/when tweaks; the specs carry many when(bit(pX)) predicates whose read keys the drivers retweak). Classified D18-family, not minimised.
STALE_SERVED UNEXPLAINED (350/326/368): counts repeat per checkpoint until the stale node is replaced; distinct events are few:
   root 2 t1 (consistent child of the root, sibling of the concurrent child) at phase 454-455, in 4 of 5 default-configuration JVMs (B-lpoff,
   B-wm1, attempt2 lpoff and attempt2 wm1; not in repro/3root-default-2), never in 3 runs without rebase or without dispose; driver actions are
   deterministic per (seed, phase), the values identical across JVMs (cached 729863718228367142 vs oracle 729864047007117110 for p127[e1,1]).
   Only t2 was updated in phase 454. Inconclusive between a concurrent-sibling effect and a harness/model artefact of the rebase; NOT claimed.
   root 1 t1 phase 203-204 (B-lpoff) and root 1 t2 phases 163-167 / 286-288 (B-lpon, repro nodispose): stale in the concurrent child or its
   sibling after when-predicate reads were retweaked in the parent (phase log: t0 add p49:=BYNAME, p71 has when(bit0(p49))): D18 mechanism
   (when-predicated by-name TweakNode keeps matching the untweaked key), classified D18. A 7-min root-1-only repro with off=when showed no
   UNEXPLAINED, but neither did the same run with when on, so the toggle is not evidence either way.
Known families seen, by name: D1 (XS), D4, D17 (CANCEL_LEAK), D18, F8, R6. Not seen in the hour: F18 TAG_DOUBLE_WRAP (tags only on the 14-prop root),
   R14 (no UPDATE_FAILED), F19.

================================================================ Other observations

verifyInvariants is only meaningful quiescent: called under traffic in the smoke runs it threw GraphInInvalidState "entry ... exists in LRU and in
   a ledger" at every sample (ledgers fill while it walks; it does not lock them despite the comment). All quiescent calls passed.
Census of the global table at 5 min: A 164 k entries, 0 invalid, 36 k done-with-exception, 57 k proxies, 81 k distinct SSCacheIDs; B 60 k entries,
   25-180 invalid, 8 k exception, 2 k TweakNodes, 1 k proxies, 50 k distinct SSCacheIDs.
